-B E F O R E - HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. ASHUTOSH KUMAR HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN DEV CHOUDHURY
07.04.2026 (Ashutosh Kumar, CJ)

We have heard Mr. R. Goswami, learned Advocate for the petitioner/National Insurance Company Limited (in short, "Insurance Company")
and Mr. H.K. Das, learned Standing Counsel, Gauhati High Court for respondent No.5.
A tragic road accident had taken place sometimes in the year 2002 where the son of respondent No.1 had died.

The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Bongaigaon passed an award sometimes in the year 2005, directing the Insurance Company to pay an amount of Rs.4,39,700/- as total compensation for the death.

This award was challenged by the Insurance Company before this Court vide WP(C)
No.7008/2005.
During the pendency of the afore-noted writ petition, the Insurance Company had deposited an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- in the High Court through a cheque on 16.11.2005.
Ultimately, the writ petition filed by the Insurance Company was dismissed.
Page No.# 3/4
The matter travelled to the Supreme Court and the dismissal order of this Court was set aside and the issue was remitted for a fresh consideration.
However, the challenge to the award was ultimately made by the Insurance Company by way of a regular statutory appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The focus of the challenge was the quantum of compensation awarded by the MACT.
The appeal was dismissed, thereby restoring the original MACT award of Rs.4,39,700/-.
The award amount was paid by the Insurance Company, which included the earlier deposited an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- in the High Court.
The interest on that amount, however, was not paid.
It is not known whether the amount which had been deposited by the Insurance Company was put to any interest bearing deposit scheme and whether it earned any interest.
In any view of the matter, with the impleadment of the Registrar General of the High Court, the matter has come before this Division Bench.

Mr. H.K. Das, learned Standing Counsel, Gauhati High Court shall take instructions in the matter and shall file an affidavit on the issue whether the deposit made by the Insurance Company in the High Court was invested in any interest bearing scheme and also the procedure adopted by the High National Insurance Company Ltd vs Manju Mazumdar And 4 Ors on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179166973/
